"You ought to explain to me that cause of the debate between those two radiant ones, which is so beautiful to hear and extremely rare even among the Purāṇas. (15)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Nārada, I shall relate this ancient narrative, by the mere hearing of which one is liberated from all sins. (16)
Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Gaṅgā—these three wives of Hari remain constantly in the presence of Hari, equal in their love for him. (17)
Once, Gaṅgā gazed upon the face of Viṣṇu;
smiling, full of desire, she looked at him again and again with sidelong glances.
Then Vibhu, beholding her face for a moment, laughed;
but upon seeing that, Lakṣmī showed forbearance, while Sarasvatī did not at all.
Padmā, who is of the nature of goodness (sattva), awakened her with a smile;
yet that speech remained possessed by anger and did not become peaceful. || 20 ||
Vāṇī, her face and eyes red, spoke to her husband;
she was enraged by the force of passion, her lower lip constantly quivering.
Sarasvatī said:
"A virtuous and most excellent man maintains an attitude of equanimity toward every woman, whereas for a wicked man, that same attitude is quite the opposite. (22)
O Gadādhara, it is known that your supreme good fortune resides in Gaṅgā, and an equal portion in Kamalā; but O Lord, there is nothing at all in me.
The highly esteemed friendship between Gaṅgā and Padmā existed;
therefore, the beloved of Hari showed forbearance toward this reversal of fortune.
"What is the use of life for me, unfortunate as I am, right here now? Wretched is the life of her who has been deprived of her husband's love. (25)
Those wise men who declare you to be of the nature of all beings are fools; they do not know the Vedas, nor do they understand your intention.
Having heard the words of Sarasvatī and seeing her filled with anger,
and having reflected upon it in his mind, he went out from the assembly hall.
When Nārāyaṇa had departed, that goddess presiding over speech, filled with rage, spoke these words— difficult to hear— to Gaṅgā in a fearless manner.
O shameless one, O lustful woman, why do you display pride toward your master? Do you wish to proclaim your own excessive good fortune as his? (29)
"Today, in the presence of Hari, I shall reduce your pride to powder.
O you who are so dear to your lover, what will your husband do for you when I have done this? (30)
Having spoken thus, she prepared to seize the hair of Gaṅgā;
Padmā, taking her stand in the middle region, restrained her. (31)
The virtuous and exceedingly powerful Vāṇī cursed that Padmā:
"Without a doubt, you shall become a tree and a river. (32)
Having seen that it is otherwise than that, you ought not to say anything;
he stands in the midst of the assembly like a tree, like a river.
Upon hearing the curse, that goddess did not curse him in return, but became enraged;
she remained right there in distress, holding her speech with her hand.
Seeing her dissatisfied, with her lower lip quivering in anger and her eyes bloodshot, Gaṅgā spoke to that goddess Padmā.
Gaṅgā said:
"Abandon this most terrible one; what will she do to me, Padmā?
She is ill-behaved, talkative, ruined, and always of a garrulous nature. (36)
This goddess, the presiding deity of speech, is constantly fond of quarreling;
such is her fitness and such is her power. (37)
Let that foul-mouthed woman likewise engage in debate with me;
she wishes to demonstrate what strength she possesses, which is my own strength. (38)
"Let everyone indeed know the power and prowess of both," having spoken thus, that goddess pronounced a curse upon Vāṇī.
"May she who cursed you become formless;
may she go down to the mortal realm where sinners dwell. (40)
"In the Kali age, he will undoubtedly take upon himself their sins.
Having heard these words, Sarasvatī cursed her. (41)
"You alone shall go to the earth; you shall receive the most grievous sin.
In the meantime, the Blessed One arrived there.
Four-armed and accompanied by four four-armed attendants,
he took Sarasvatī by the hand and placed her upon his chest.
The omniscient one awakened the ancient, all-encompassing knowledge;
having heard their secret concerning the curse and the quarrel.
The All-pervading Lord spoke these timely words to those distressed women;
the Blessed One said: "O auspicious Lakṣmī, go with a portion of yourself to the house of Dharmadhvaja."
Born from the earth through an improper union, you shall become his daughter;
and there, by the fault of fate, you shall attain the state of a tree.
"Having first become the beloved wife of the Asura Śaṅkhacūḍa, who is a portion of myself, you shall afterwards become my wife; of this there is no doubt. (47)
"O fair-faced one, go quickly to Bhārata in the form of a river by the name Tulasī, who purifies the three worlds, and do so through a portion of yourself."
"O Bhāratī, by virtue of my curse, become Padmāvatī by name;
O Gaṅgā, you shall later depart as a portion [of yourself], the purifier of the universe. (49)
Due to the curse of Bhāratī, the Bhārata [Purāṇa] exists for the burning away of the sins of sinners;
by the well-conceived penance of Bhagīratha, it was brought down. 50.
"Purified by the name Bhāgīrathī, you shall exist upon the surface of the earth;
by my command, you shall become the wife of the ocean, who is a portion of myself. (51)
O Goddess of the Gods, O Sarasvatī, go to Bhārata by means of a portion of yourself, through a digit of King Śantanu, who is a part of my own energy, due to the curse of Gaṅgā.
O Acyuta, enjoy the fruit of this quarrel with your two co-wives;
and you yourself become the beloved of Brahmā in the abode of Brahmā.
"Let Gaṅgā go to the abode of Śiva; let Padmā remain here, peaceful, free from anger, my devotee, and embodied as the quality of purity (sattva). (54)
She is a great saintly woman, highly fortunate, virtuous, and a practitioner of dharma;
by a portion of her own essence, all women have become most righteous and devoted to their husbands.
They were peaceful in appearance, possessed of excellent conduct, and honored in every household;
they had three wives of virtuous character, as well as three servants and kinsmen.
It is certain that these [omens] are contrary to the Vedas and do not bestow auspiciousness;
for those householders in whose home the man is under the control of the woman, as if she were his equal, [misfortune follows]. (57)
Their birth is fruitless and at every step they encounter misfortune, for he whose wife is foul-mouthed, of corrupt womb, and fond of quarreling. (58)
Therefore, one should go to the forest; the great forest is better than one's home, for there is the attainment of water, dry land, and fruits. (59)
There, as well as in their own homes, such things are not always easily obtained;
indeed, it would be better for them to dwell in fire or to find comfort in the presence of predatory beasts.
Even greater than that, O fair-faced one, is the certain suffering for men in the presence of a wicked woman;
the flame of disease or the flame of poison is better for men. (61)
The flame from the mouths of wicked women is worse than death;
for men conquered by women, purification ends in ashes and is unstable.
On whichever day one performs an action, he shall not partake of its fruit;
being censured both here and in the next world, he shall go to hell in every respect. || 63 ||
He who is bereft of fame and renown is indeed dead even while living;
and for many co-wives, there can be no abiding in prosperity in one place. (64)
One with a single wife is happy, never one with many wives.
Go to the abode of Śiva, O Gaṅgā; go to the abode of Brahmā, O Sarasvatī! (65)
Let the virtuous Kamalālayā remain here in my house;
for he whose wife is easy to manage, virtuous, and devoted to her husband, [is truly blessed]. 66.
In this world he enjoys happiness in heaven, and in the next world he attains dharma and liberation;
he whose wife is devoted to her husband is liberated, pure, and happy. But he who is the husband of an ill-behaved wife is as if dead while living, impure, and miserable.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Descent of Lakṣmī, Gaṅgā, and Sarasvatī onto the Earth," in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighteen thousand verses.
The Description of the Removal of the Curse from Gaṅgā and Others.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having spoken thus, O Nārada, the Lord of the worlds became silent.
The goddesses wept excessively, embracing one another. || 1 ||
Having beheld them all, they spoke in turn to the Lord,
trembling with tears in their eyes due to both grief and fear.
Sarasvatī said:
"O Lord, grant us freedom from this curse, which has caused misery since birth.
Abandoned by their virtuous husbands, how can those women continue to live? (3)
"I shall certainly cast off my body through yoga in Bhārata;
for one who is exceedingly elevated must surely fall, this is certain. (4)
Gangā said: "O Lord of the World, by what offense have I been abandoned by you?
I shall give up my life; let me incur the death of one who is innocent. (5)
Whatever man on earth abandons a faultless wife—
even if he were the Lord of All— he goes to a terrible hell.
Padmā said:
"O Lord, you are the very embodiment of goodness; how then can there be anger in you? O Master, show favor toward your two wives; forgiveness is the highest virtue."
Due to the curse of Bhāratī, I shall indeed descend with a portion of myself into Bhārata;
for how long will my stay there be, and when shall I behold your feet? (8)
Sinners will deliver their sins [to me] immediately upon bathing and immersion;
by what means shall I be liberated from them so that I may come to your abode? (9)
O Acyuta, having enjoyed the form of Tulasī as a portion [of you], when shall I, the virtuous daughter of Dharmadhvaja, attain your lotus feet?
"I shall become a tree-form, the presiding deity of you;
O ocean of compassion, tell me when you will deliver me. (11)
If the Gaṅgā goes to Bhārata due to the curse of Sarasvatī, when, freed from that curse and from sin, will she attain you? (12)
If the Goddess of Speech shall go to Bhārata due to the curse of Gaṅgā, when will she, having been released from that curse, regain her place with you? (13)
O Lord, you speak of going to that voice, or to the abode of Brahmā, or to the Gaṅgā, or to the temple of Śiva; therefore, please forgive those words of yours.
Having spoken thus, Kamalā grasped the foot of her beloved, bowed down, and, encircling him with her hair, wept again and again. (15)
(Padmanābha, placing Padmā upon his chest, spoke to her with a face brightened by a slight smile, being intent on bestowing grace upon his devotees.)
The Blessed Lord said:
"O Sovereign of the Gods, I shall carry out your word and my own word as well;
I shall establish equality between them. Listen, O lotus-eyed one! (16)
"Let the Goddess of Speech go to the land of Bhārata in a portion in the form of a river;
let half of her remain herself in my abode, the seat of Brahmā. (17)
"Since that Gaṅgā was brought by Bhagīratha and will go to the land of Bhārata to purify the three worlds, let her herself remain in my house. (18)
Right there, she shall obtain the rare crown of Candramauli;
thereafter, though already pure by nature, she will become exceedingly purified. (19)
"O lovely-eyed one, go to Bhārata by means of a minute fraction of a part; there you shall take the form of the river Padmāvatī and the Tulasī tree. (20)
"When five thousand years of the Kali age have passed, your liberation shall come;
you and all the rivers shall come to my abode. (21)
Prosperity is the cause of misfortune for all embodied beings;
without misfortune, who could possess greatness in this world of lotus-born Brahmā? (22)
And for the virtuous who worship my mantra, through bathing and immersion, as well as by seeing and touching you, there shall be liberation from sin. (23)
O beautiful one, whatever innumerable holy places exist upon the earth shall become purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (24)
Devotees who worship my mantra wander throughout Bhārata in order to purify and deliver this most sacred earth. (25)
Wherever my devotees reside and wash their feet, that place shall certainly become a great sacred ford (tīrtha) and exceedingly pure. || 26 ||

The killer of a woman, the killer of a cow, the ungrateful, the killer of a Brahmin, and the violator of the guru’s bed—such a person becomes purified and liberated while living merely by the touch and sight of my devotee. || 27 ||
One who has neglected the Ekādaśī fast, one who has omitted the twilight prayers, an atheist, or even a killer of a human being becomes purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (28)
One who lives by the sword, one who lives by ink, a washerman, a village beggar, or a bullock-driver becomes purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (29)
A betrayer of trust, a slayer of friends, a giver of false testimony, or one who takes food from such a person, becomes purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (30)
Even an extremely grave defiler, a paramour, the husband of an unchaste woman,
or the son of a low-caste woman, becomes purified by the touch or sight of one devoted to me.
Even the cook of Śūdras, Devala, and the village priest shall become pure by the mere touch and sight of my devotee, even if they have not received initiation. (32)
One's father, mother, wife, brother, son, daughter, the family of the preceptor, sister, and a blind relative—[these one should support]. || 33 ||
O beautiful one, he who does not support his mother-in-law and father-in-law is a perpetrator of a great sin; yet he is purified by the touch and sight of my devotee.
Even a Brahmin who destroys an Aśvattha tree, who reviles my devotees, or who eats the food of a Śūdra, becomes purified by the sight of my devotee. (35)
One who steals the property of the gods, one who misappropriates the property of Brahmins, a seller of lac, iron, and mercury, as well as one who sells his own daughter; || 36 ||
Even those who have committed great sins, as well as those who burn the corpses of Śūdras—these shall become purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (37)
Mahālakṣmī said:
O you who are eager to bestow grace upon devotees, tell me the characteristics of those devotees by whose sight and touch even the lowest of men are instantly purified. (38)
Devoid of devotion to Hari and possessed of great egoism,
they are rogues devoted to self-praise, deceitful, and revilers of the virtuous.
All sacred fords are purified by bathing and immersion in them;
and by the dust of their feet, the earth is sanctified by the water used for washing their feet.
For those who desire to see or touch [them] in Bhārata, the supreme gain for all is the company of Vaiṣṇavas. (41)
For holy fords are not made of water, nor are gods made of clay or stone;
yet those who are devotees of Viṣṇu purify even in an instant—how wonderful! (42)
Sūta said:
Having heard the words of Mahālakṣmī, the beloved of Lakṣmī (Viṣṇu) smiled and,
being the most excellent one, began to explain the hidden truth.
The Blessed Lord said: O Lakṣmī, the characteristics of devotees are hidden in the Śrutis and Purāṇas;
they are meritorious in nature, destroyers of sin, bestowers of happiness, and granters of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
This essential matter, which must be kept secret and should not be spoken of to the wicked, I shall tell you, for you are pure and as dear to me as my own life; listen. (45)
The Vedas declare that he into whose ear the Viṣṇu-mantra falls from the mouth of the Guru is indeed pure and the best among men. (46)
A hundred generations of men from before, as well as those born simultaneously with him—whether they be in heaven or in hell—attain liberation at that very moment. || 47 ||
By whomever birth has been obtained, wherever, or among whatever beings—
those who are liberated while living are purified and go at the time of death to the abode of Hari.
A mortal endowed with devotion to me is liberated and becomes possessed of my qualities;
he whose conduct is dependent on my qualities and who is constantly immersed in my stories [is likewise freed]. (49)
Merely by hearing of my virtues, he was filled with joy, his hair stood on end, his voice became choked with emotion, his eyes were filled with tears, and he was completely forgetful of himself. (50)
He does not desire happiness, liberation, the fourfold states such as *sālokya*, nor even the status of Brahmā or immortality; his only desire is in my service. (51)
He does not desire even in a dream the extremely difficult-to-attain status of Indra, Manu, or Brahmā, nor the enjoyments of the kingdom of heaven and other such realms.
Devotees wander throughout Bhārata; such a birth is very difficult to obtain.
They are constantly filled with joy by hearing of my qualities through melodious songs. 53.
"Having purified the earth, they go to Nara, my abode which is a sacred ford (tīrtha).
Thus everything was told; O Padmā, do what is appropriate.
By his command, they did so, and Hari remained upon his comfortable seat.

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Removal of the Curse of Gaṅgā and Others," in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighteen thousand verses.
In the dialogue between Nārāyaṇa and Nārada, the description of the majesty of Kali:
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Sarasvatī came to the meritorious field in Bhārata.
By the curse of Gaṅgā, he himself remained in a portion within the station of Hari.
Having gone to Bhārata, Bhāratī and Brāhmī, the beloved of Brahmā, became the presiding deity of speech; for that reason, she is celebrated as Vāṇī.
A lake is seen everywhere, as is a stream; because Hari possesses such lakes (saras), this river is therefore called Sarasvatī by that name.
And that river Sarasvatī is a sacred ford (tīrtha) of supreme purity;
she has the nature of a blazing fire for the burning away of the sins of the wicked.
Subsequently, O Nārada, she was brought to the earth by Bhagīratha;
yet, due to the curse of Vāṇī, she went there only in a partial form.
At that very moment, the omnipresent Śiva bore her upon his head;
he was able to endure her force only through the prayer of the Earth.
Padmā departed with a portion [of herself], and she became the river Padmāvatī;
due to the curse of Bhāratī, she herself remained in the abode of Hari in Bhārata.
Then, by another portion of herself, she took birth in Bhārata as Lakṣmī,
the daughter of Dharmadhvaja, renowned as Tulasī.
Formerly, due to the curse of Sarasvatī, and later due to the curse of Hari, she,
the purifier of the universe, became a tree by means of a portion of her essence.
Having remained in Bhārata for five thousand years of Kali,
they abandoned their river-forms and went to the abode of Śrī Hari.
All those holy places that exist, excluding Kāśī and Vṛndāvana,
shall depart for Vaikuṇṭha along with them by the command of Hari.
The Śālagrāma, Śakti, Śiva, Jagannātha, and Bhārata—
these abandon the world at the end of ten thousand years of the Kali age and depart for their own abode.
The virtuous ones, as well as the ancient conch shells used for the ancestral rites of libation (śrāddha-tarpaṇa),
and the rituals prescribed in the Vedas, all went along with them.
Devapūjā, Devanāma, and Tatkīrtiguṇakīrtana, as well as the Vedāṅgas and the Śāstras, went along with them. (14)
Peace, the true dharma, the Vedas, the village deities, religious vows, austerity, and fasting—all these likewise departed together with them. || 15 ||
All will be devoted to left-handed practices (vāmācāra) and filled with falsehood and deceit;
thereafter, worship devoid of Tulasī shall prevail.
Thereafter, all people will become deceitful, cruel, hypocritical, and possessed of great egotism; they will be thieves and harmful. (17)
Thereafter, there will be the distinction of men, the distinction of women, marriage without fear, and the distinction between property and its owner.
All men are under the sway of women, and in every house there are unchaste women who constantly strike their husbands with threats and reproaches.
The mistress of the house and the housewife are superior to the master of the house, while the latter is inferior even to his servants;
likewise, the mother-in-law and the father-in-law are equal to a servant-girl and a slave respectively.
In the house of the powerful, the kinsmen related by birth and those related by learning do not even engage in conversation together. (21)
Just as people are familiar with the world, so too are men's kinsmen;
men are incapable of performing any action without the command of women. 22.
The Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras will be devoid of their proper birth-status and conduct;
their twilight devotions and sacred threads will undoubtedly be lost. (23)
The four castes will adopt the conduct of barbarians;
they will study the scriptures of barbarians, having abandoned their own scriptures. (24)
In the Kali age, the lineages of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas become servants of Śūdras;
they will all be cooks, washermen, and ox-drivers.
All people were bereft of truth, the earth was devoid of crops, the trees were without fruit, and women were without offspring. (26)
Cows devoid of milk, milk from which butter has been extracted, a husband and wife lacking affection, and householders bereft of truth; || 27 ||
The kings will be devoid of majesty, and the subjects will be oppressed by taxes;
the great rivers, the ponds, the caves, and other such places will be devoid of water.
Deprived of dharma and deprived of merit, even the four social orders (varṇas) [perish];
beyond that, not even a single meritorious person remains among hundreds of thousands. 29.
Thereafter, men, women, and children will become contemptible and deformed in appearance; furthermore, there will be evil rumors and loathsome sounds.
Some villages and cities were terrifying and devoid of people;
some were occupied by only a few huts and a single person.
Forests will arise within villages and cities;
all people who dwell in the forest will be oppressed by taxes.
Crops will grow even in ponds and rivers;
and in the Kali age, those born of noble lineages will become degraded.
O Nārada, there will be deceitful rogues who speak falsely and utter untruths; and even the most excellent fields will be devoid of crops. (34)
The citizens were base and excellent, wealthy and devoted to the gods, as well as atheists, violent, devoid of compassion, and murderers of men. (35)
In the Kali age, men and women everywhere will be dwarfish, afflicted by diseases, short-lived, plagued by ailments, and deprived of youth. (36)
In the sixteenth year, women have grey hair; at twenty, they are considered very old;
and at eight years of age, a young woman is possessed of menses and becomes pregnant. || 37 ||
In the Kali age, every woman who gives birth at the end of her year [of marriage], or one who reaches old age at sixteen, or even one who has a husband and sons— all such women are considered barren.
All four castes who sell their daughters, those who have sexual intercourse with their mother, their wife, or their daughter-in-law, and those who eat food provided by such adulterers; || 39 ||
In the Kali age, there will be those who take wives or sisters as mistresses for their livelihood, and those who sell the names of Hari. (40)
Having himself bestowed gifts for the sake of increasing his fame,
he will subsequently transgress his own gift.
He will transgress everything— the way of the gods, the way of Brahman, the way of the teacher’s household, and whatever has been given, whether by himself or by another.
Some were those who went to virgins, some went to mothers-in-law,
some went to daughters-in-law, and some indeed went to all women.
In the Kali age, there will be some who approach their sisters, those who approach their co-wives, mothers, and even the wives of their brothers.
They will commit forbidden sexual acts in every household;
abandoning their mothers' wombs, they will procreate everywhere.
In the Kali age, there is no final determination regarding wives and husbands, nor concerning offspring, villages, and especially property. (46)
All were speakers of falsehoods, all were thieves and libertines;
they were mutual destroyers and all were slayers of men. (47)
The lineages of the Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas will become sinful;
they will engage in the trade of lac, metals, juices, and salt.
Those of the Brahmin lineage who ride oxen, those who burn the corpses of Śūdras, those who eat the food of Śūdras—all of them, and all of them, are devoted to Vṛṣalīs. 49.

Those who have abandoned the five sacrifices, those who eat on the night of the new moon (Kuhū), those who are devoid of the sacrificial thread, and those who lack the twilight prayers and ritual purity; || 50 ||
A wanton woman, one who lives by usury, a procuress, and a menstruating woman shall become the cook in the kitchens of the Brahmins. (51)
In the Kali age, there is no restriction regarding foods, nor particularly regarding wombs; among the stages of life and among people, all are considered Mlecchas.
Thus, when the Kali age has fully set in, everything shall become filled with barbarians;
trees will be no more than the span of a hand, and men will be no taller than a thumb.
The son of the brahmin Viṣṇuyaśas will be Kalki,
a portion of a fraction of Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, the best among the strong.
With a long sword and riding a long-necked steed,
he shall, within three nights, rid the earth of Mlecchas.
Having made the earth free of barbarians, he will disappear;
and the earth will become kingless and seized by bandits.
The earth, drenched by rain-showers of massive proportions for six nights,
will become empty of people, empty of trees, and empty of houses.
And then, O Sage, twelve suns will rise;
by their combined splendor, the earth shall reach a state of total desiccation.
When the invincible Kali age has passed and the Kṛta age has begun, Dharma, endowed with austerity and goodness, will become complete once again.
On this earth, there were ascetic and most righteous Brāhmaṇas who were knowers of the Vedas;
and in every house, there were women who were devoted to their husbands and most virtuous.
All the kings, being Kṣatriyas, were devoted to the Brahmins, high-minded, majestic, most righteous, and always engaged in meritorious deeds. || 61 ||
The Vaiśyas were devoted to trade, devoted to the Brahmins, and righteous;
and the Śūdras were of meritorious character, most virtuous, and devoted to the service of the Brahmins.
The lineages of the Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas were all devoted to the Goddess;
they were all intent upon the mantras of the Goddess and dedicated to the meditation on the Goddess.
In the Kṛta Yuga, men who were knowers of the Śruti, Smṛti, and Purāṇas approached their wives only during the proper season; there was not even a trace of unrighteousness, for dharma was complete.
In the Tretā age, Dharma stands on three feet; then in the Dvāpara, it stands on two;
when the Kali age has occurred, it stands on one foot, and after that, there is the total disappearance of all things.
Likewise, O Brahmin, seven days (vāras) are recorded, as well as sixteen lunar days (tithis);
similarly, there are twelve months and exactly six seasons. || 66 ||
There are two fortnights and two solstices;
a day consists of four watches, and a night likewise consists of four watches; a month consists of thirty days. (67)
The year is to be known as fivefold according to the sequence of the rules for the calculation of time;
just as they come and go, so too is the cycle of the four ages (yugas). 68.
When a full year for humans and a day and night for the gods has passed—that is, when three hundred and sixty years of humans have elapsed as one *yuga*—[the dissolution occurs]. (69)
And a Yuga of the gods should be known as the opinion of those who understand the calculation of time;
however, a Manvantara consists of seventy-one such divine Yugas. (70)
The lifespan of the Lord of Śacī (Indra) should be known as equal to a Manvantara;
when twenty-eight Indras have passed, it constitutes a day and night of Brahmā.
When one hundred and eight years have passed, there occurs the fall of Brahmā;
that should be known as the elemental dissolution (prākṛta-pralaya), wherein the earth is no longer perceived.
When all things were submerged in water, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva,
and all the wise sages were dissolved into the Truth, the conscious Self.
Right there primordial nature (prakṛti) is dissolved; therein lies the dissolution of nature (prākṛtika-laya).
O Sage, when this natural dissolution has occurred and Brahmā has fallen [into sleep], [the cycle continues].
O Sage, even a mere moment of time is said to be the [duration] of the Śrī Devī;
in this way, all entire cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍas) perish.
In the interval of a single blink of an eye, through the process of creation once again—how many kinds of creation are there, or how many kinds of dissolution as well? (76)
O Nārada, what man knows the number of the kalpas that have passed and those yet to come, as well as the creations, the dissolutions, and the cosmic eggs?
What man can know the number of those beginning with Brahmā within the cosmic egg?
He alone is the sole Lord of all the cosmic eggs. (78)
The Supreme Self of all bears the form of existence, consciousness, and bliss;
Brahmā and the others are His portions, and the Great Virāṭ is a portion of Him.
And his portion was Virāṭ Kṣudra; she herself is this supreme Prakṛti. From her presence, Ardhanārīśvara was born thereafter.
That very Kṛṣṇa became twofold, appearing both as two-armed and four-armed;
he is four-armed in Vaikuṇṭha, while in Goloka he himself is two-armed.
Everything from Brahmā down to a blade of grass is composed of primordial nature (prakṛti);
whatever is created from primordial nature is entirely perishable.
Such is the cause of creation: the Truth, eternal, and everlasting;
consisting of His own will, the Supreme Brahman, devoid of qualities, and beyond primordial nature (prakṛti).
Free from limiting adjuncts and formless, yet eager to bestow grace upon devotees, He creates the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) through whose knowledge the lotus-born Brahmā comes into being. 84.
Śiva is indeed the conqueror of death, the destroyer, and the knower of all beings;
through his knowledge and his austerity, he is the Lord of All and possesses great ascetic power.
Endowed with great majesty, he is all-knowing and all-seeing;
he is all-pervading, the protector of all, and the bestower of all perfections.
By devotion to whom and by service to whom Viṣṇu, the glorious Lord of all, as well as Mahāmāyā, the Sovereign Goddess who consists of all powers and is primordial nature (prakṛti), [are won]. 87.
She alone is declared to be the Blessed Lady, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss;
by whose knowledge, by whose austerity, by whose devotion, and by whose service [all is attained]. 88.
Sāvitrī is the mother of the gods and the presiding deity of the Vedas;
she is to be worshipped by the twice-born who know the Vedas, for it is through her service that one attains knowledge of the Veda. (89)
She is the presiding goddess of all sciences, the supreme object of worship for the wise;
by her service and by her ascetic penance, she is honored throughout the entire universe. (90)
She is the presiding deity of every village, the bestower of all prosperity, the sovereign of all, worthy of worship by all, and the giver of sons to everyone. || 91 ||
She is praised by all, she is omniscient, and she is the destroyer of the suffering of all who are in distress;
she is born from the left shoulder of Kṛṣṇa and is the presiding deity of Kṛṣṇa’s life-force.
Through her service to the power of Rādhikā with love, she possesses a life-force superior to Kṛṣṇa’s, a form that is most excellent, and supreme good fortune, honor, and dignity. (93)
Through her service, she attained the status of wife and the position of standing upon Kṛṣṇa’s chest;
previously, she had performed penance on the Śataśṛṅga mountain.
And for a thousand divine years, she remained solely for the sake of obtaining a husband;
then, when Śakti’s grace had arisen, she beheld her who was like a digit of the moon.
The omnipresent Lord Kṛṣṇa, placing her upon his chest, wept out of compassion and granted her a supreme boon, the most difficult of all to obtain.
"Abide upon my chest as my eternal devotee, endowed with good fortune, honor, love, and respect. (97)
"You are my most excellent and eldest, the dearest of all women; you are the most distinguished and most venerable, praised and honored by me. (98)
"O beloved of my life, I am forever to be accomplished for you and under your control," having said this, the Lord of the World then transformed himself into a woman.
And he made that beloved of his life free from rival wives;
and whatever other goddesses there were, they too were honored through service to Śakti.
O Sage, whatever kind of austerity those women practiced, they obtained a corresponding fruit;
having performed penance for a thousand divine years on the Himālaya mountain, they attained their goal.
And Durgā, having meditated upon that state, became worthy of worship by all;
and Sarasvatī, having performed austerities on Mount Gandhamādana, [attained her goal].
Having performed austerities at Puṣkara for a hundred divine yugas, she became Lakṣmī, worthy of the worship of all, for a hundred thousand divine years.
Through her service to the Goddess, she became the bestower of all prosperity;
having performed austerities at Malaya, Sāvitrī became worthy of worship and salutation.
O Lord, in the past, Śaṅkara meditated upon that state for sixty thousand divine years and performed austerities for a hundred manvantaras.
For a hundred manvantaras, Brahmā indeed chanted the Śakti-mantra;
for a hundred manvantaras, Viṣṇu, having performed penance, became the protector.
Having performed supreme austerity for ten Manvantaras, Śrī Kṛṣṇa attained the divine Goloka, where he indeed rejoices even today.
Having performed penance for ten Manvantaras endowed with devotion,
he indeed became the life-force of all, worthy of worship by all, and the support of all.
Thus, by the ascetic penance of the Goddess, all the gods were honored;
likewise, the sages, the Manus, the kings, and the Brahmins were also honored.
Thus I have related to you everything from the Purāṇa according to tradition, just as it was learned from the mouth of my guru. What more do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of Kali," in the dialogue between Nārāyaṇa and Nārada, within the ninth book of the Śrīmad Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighteen thousand verses.
In the *Bhūmistotravarṇana*,
Nārada said:
"In the mere twinkling of an eye of the Goddess, there was even the falling of Brahmā."
The falling away of that [state] is proclaimed as the natural dissolution (prākṛtika-pralaya). || 1 ||
And regarding the elemental dissolution (prākṛta-pralaya) which has been described, there the earth is not perceived;
all worlds are submerged in water, and everyone is dissolved into the Supreme Self.
Where has Vasundharā vanished, and where does she now abide? How did she manifest once again at the time of the creation of the universe?
How did that blessed, venerable, all-supporting, and victorious one come to be?
Tell me her story of birth, which is the cause of auspiciousness.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: According to the Śruti, in every primordial creation, the birth of all beings is from the Goddess;
likewise, their manifestation and disappearance occur in all dissolutions.
Listen to the account of the birth of Vasudhā, which is the cause of all auspiciousness,
the destroyer of obstacles, the eradicator of sins, and the increaser of merit.
"Aha! Some say that the earth became blessed by the fat of Madhu and Kaiṭabha; hear now what contradicts that. (7)
In former times, when they were gratified by his prowess in battle and his splendor, those two said to Viṣṇu:
"We two are not to be slain as long as the earth is covered with water. (8)
During their lifetime, she was clearly not perceptible to them;
therefore, a difference arose between them after their death.
"She is renowned as Medinī"—listen now to this doctrine concerning why she was so called:
because she was formerly washed by the waters and subsequently nourished by fat (medas).
I shall relate to you that birth which is meaningful and auspicious in every way;
it is that which was heard of old as declared by the Śrutis and from the mouth of Dharma at Puṣkara.
In the course of time, the mind of the Great Virāṭ, who had long remained clearly situated within the water, certainly became pervasive throughout all his limbs.
And that [water], O Sage, having entered into all the pores of those hairs,
after a long time, subsequently became the earth.
And she always remained within wells for each and every hair,
appearing and disappearing again and again, filled with water.
Manifested at the time of creation, she stands upon its waters;
and at the time of dissolution, having become concealed, she remains within the water.
In every universe, there is an earth endowed with mountains and forests, joined by the seven oceans and possessed of the seven continents. || 16 ||
Joined with Hemādri and Meru, and accompanied by the planets, the moon, and the sun, as well as by the gods such as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, and by the worlds at his command; (17)
It is endowed with sacred fords, joined with the meritorious land of Bhārata, possessed of golden ground, and furnished with the seven heavens. || 18 ||
There are seven netherworlds (pātāla) beneath that, and above it, up to the world of Brahmā (brahmaloka), lies the world of Dhruva; indeed, the entire universe is contained therein.
Thus, all these various things fashioned upon the earth are perishable; indeed, all these diverse things are artificial.
During the elemental dissolution, at the fall of Brahmā,
and during the creation of Mahāvirāṭ and the rest, he was created by Kṛṣṇa through his own self.
Both maintenance and dissolution are eternal, along with the quarters, time, and the Lord;
she is the eternal presiding goddess, worshipped by the gods in the Vārāha [Kalpa].
She is the wife of Viṣṇu in his Boar incarnation, as acknowledged by the sages, Manu, the Brahmins, the Gandharvas, and others, and is thus sanctioned by the Vedas. 23.
His son is to be known as Maṅgala, and Ghaṭeśa is the son of Maṅgala.
Nārada said:
In what form was the Earth worshipped by the gods during the Vārāha [kalpa]?

And Vārāhī is indeed in Vārāha; she is the reality (satī) who is the refuge of all through all [means], born from the primordial nature (mūlaprakṛti) by way of the process of quintuplication (pañcīkaraṇa). || 25 ||
O Lord, tell us also the procedure for her worship, both below and above in manifold ways, as well as the auspicious birth and dwelling place of Maṅgala himself.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
In the Vārāha-kalpa, Varāha was formerly praised by Brahmā;
having slain Hiraṇyākṣa, he lifted up the earth from the netherworld (rasātala).
He placed her in the water like a lotus leaf upon a lake;
there, Brahmā himself fashioned the entire enchanting universe.
Having seen that presiding goddess filled with desire, the Lord Hari, the lover,
assumed the form of a boar, possessing a splendor equal to ten million suns.
Having assumed every art of love and a most enchanting form,
he sported in secret day and night for a divine year.
From the touch of the blissful enjoyment, Sundarī fell into a swoon;
for the union of the clever with the clever bestows supreme happiness. (31)
Due to the constant contact with her body, Viṣṇu was not aware of day or night;
at the end of a year, regaining his senses, the lover abandoned the woman of desire.
He playfully assumed the form of a boar, his former shape,
and having meditated upon that virtuous Goddess Earth, he performed her worship.
Having worshipped her with incense, lamps, food offerings, vermilion, ointments, garments, flowers, and oblations, Hari spoke to her.
The Blessed One said: "O auspicious one, become the support of all, being honored by everyone—by sages, Manus, gods, Siddhas, Dānavas, and others—for your own happiness. (35)

On the day of the Āmbuvācī sacrifice, at the commencement of building a house, at the time of entering it, at the start of constructing a step-well or a pond, and in the undertaking of agricultural work within the home; || 36 ||
By my boon, the gods and others shall perform worship of you;
those fools who do not do so shall go to hell.
Vasudhā said:
"O Blessed One, at your command, I carry everything—the entire universe with its moving and non-moving beings—merely as a sport, in the form of a boar. (38)
A pearl-oyster, an image of Hari, a Śiva-liṅga, Pārvatī, a conch, a lamp, a yantra, as well as a ruby and a diamond; || 39 ||
A sacred thread, a flower, a book, a tulasī leaf, a rosary, a garland of flowers, camphor, and gold; || 40 ||
"O Blessed One, listen; I am distressed because I am unable to carry these: gorocanā, sandalwood, and likewise the water from a śālagrāma. (41)
The Blessed Lord said:
O beautiful one, those fools who shall offer these substances to you will go to the Kālasūtra hell for a hundred divine years.
Having spoken thus, O Nārada, the Blessed One became silent;
by that embryo, the planet Maṅgala became radiant with splendor.
At the command of Hari, they all performed worship of the Earth and praised her with hymns and meditations prescribed in the Kaṇva recension.
They offered the food offering and other items with the root mantra;
thus praised and worshipped throughout the three worlds, she became truly honored.
Nārada said:
Tell me, what is her meditation, what is her hymn of praise, and what is her root mantra?
It is hidden in all the Purāṇas; I have a great curiosity to hear it.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: In the beginning, the goddess Earth was worshipped by Varāha;
thereafter, the Earth was indeed cleansed by Brahmā. (47)
Then, O Nārada, listen as I shall speak of the meditation, the hymn of praise, and the mantra [performed] by all the lords of sages, the Manus, Mānavas, and others. 48.
"Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ vasudhāyai svāhā"—by this mantra she was worshipped by Viṣṇu in ancient times.
She possesses the luster of the color of a white lotus, and her face resembles the autumnal moon. (49)
Her entire body was anointed with sandalwood paste, and she was adorned with jewel ornaments;
she was the receptacle of jewels, the womb of jewels, and endowed with a mine of jewels.
"I worship her who wears garments as pure as fire, who is smiling, and who is saluted;
by this meditation, that Goddess became worshipped by all. (51)
"Listen, O best of Brahmins, to this hymn of praise as it is indeed declared in the Kaṇva recension.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Victory! Victory! O you who are the receptacle of water, whose nature is water, and who bestow water!"
O you who are born from the sacrificial boar, grant us victory, O bringer of victory!
O auspicious one, O support of auspiciousness, O source of well-being, O bestower of auspiciousness!
O Sovereign of Auspiciousness, grant me auspiciousness for the sake of prosperity in this world;
O Support of All, Omniscient One, endowed with all powers! (54)
O Goddess who grants all desires, grant me everything that is desired in this world; O eternal one, whose nature is merit and who is the seed-form of all merits! 55.
O refuge of merit, abode of the meritorious, source of merit;
O you who are the repository of all crops, enriched by all crops, the giver of all crops! 56.
O Earth, who at the time of harvest takest away all crops, who art the soul of all crops, who art the very essence of the earth, and whose ultimate refuge is the protector of the earth! || 57 ||
O Giver of Land, grant land that brings happiness to the rulers of the earth!
Whoever recites this hymn of great merit upon rising in the morning, [shall obtain such land]. (58)
For ten million births, he shall become a powerful lord of kings;
by reading this, people obtain the merit produced by the gift of land.
One is liberated from the sin of seizing land; there is no doubt in this matter.
One is certainly freed from the sin of making land into a watercourse.
He is certainly liberated from the sin of digging a well on another's land;
he is liberated from the sin of seizing another's property—of this there is no doubt. (61)
O Sage, even one who has committed the sin of abandoning effort on the ground is liberated from that sin by placing lamps and other offerings upon the ground, and by the recitation of this hymn.
One obtains the merit of a hundred horse-sacrifices; there is no doubt about this.
This great hymn to Bhūmidevī brings about all auspiciousness. (63)
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Hymn to the Earth," in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighteen thousand verses.
In the narrative of Pṛthivī, there is a description of the attainment of the fruit of hell.
Nārada said: "The merit produced by the gift of land, and the sin resulting from its seizure."
Sin arises from seizing the property of others, as well as from digging a well on another's land.
I wish to hear with diligence about the sin incurred by digging the earth on a day called Ambuvācī, by the abandonment of semen, and by the installation of lamps and other such objects.
Or whatever other sin born of the earth may exist that you ask about another—tell me its remedy, O best among those who know the Vedas. (3)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
He who gives even a piece of land measuring a vitasti in Bhārata to a Brāhmaṇa purified by the twilight prayers goes to the abode of Śiva.
And he who gives land rich with all kinds of crops to a Brāhmaṇa remains in the abode of Viṣṇu for as many years as there are particles of dust in that land.
He who gives a village, land, and grain to a Brāhmaṇa is liberated from all sins, and both [the giver and the recipient] stand before the Goddess.
And he who at that time virtuously approves of the gift of land shall go to Vaikuṇṭha, accompanied by his friends and kinsmen.
Whoever seizes the property granted for the sustenance of Brahmins, whether given by himself or by another,
shall dwell in the Kālasūtra hell as long as the moon and sun endure.
There, his sons, grandsons, and descendants shall be deprived of land, struck down by misfortune, childless, and impoverished; and he goes to the terrible Raurava hell.
He who obstructs the path of cows and yet gives grain [as an offering] remains in Kumbhīpāka for a hundred divine years.
He who diverts a cow-pen or a pond and gives the water to his crops on the path remains in the Sword-Leaf Hell for as long as the fourteen Indras endure.
He who bathes in another's well without having first removed the five lumps of earth [from his own body] falls into hell, and his bath is indeed fruitless.
And he who, being lustful, discharges his semen on the ground in a secluded place,
remains in the Raurava hell for as many years as there are particles of dust on that ground.
The man who performs the ritual of digging the earth on Ambuvācī goes to the world of worm-bites, and his stay there lasts for four yugas.
The fool who constructs a well in another's ruined well, or who provides a lotus pond where a lotus pond has perished; || 15 ||
All his merit shall go to another, and he shall go to the Taptakuṇḍa hell;
there he remains tormented for as long as the reign of fourteen Indras.
And by clearing away the mud from another's pond and cleaning it, a man shall dwell in the world of Brahmā for as many years as there are particles of dust removed. || 17 ||
That foolish man who performs a śrāddha without first offering a ball of rice (piṇḍa) to his father, the lord of the earth, certainly goes to hell. (18)
He who offers a lamp upon the ground shall be blind for seven births;
and by placing a conch shell upon the ground, one may suffer from leprosy in a future life. (19)
He who places pearls, rubies, emeralds, gold, and likewise gems upon the ground shall be blind for seven births.
He who installs a Śiva-liṅga or an image of Śiva on the earth remains for a hundred manvantaras as food for worms.
He who offers a conch, a mechanical device, water from a stone vessel, or a flower such as a tulasī leaf upon the ground, will certainly remain in hell.
That fool who offers a rosary, a garland of flowers, camphor, or yellow pigment upon the ground certainly goes to hell. (23)
Having placed sandalwood, rudrākṣa, and the root of kuśa grass upon the ground, one shall dwell in hell for the duration of a manvantara.
A person should place a book and a sacred thread upon the ground;
for him, there shall be no birth in another life within the womb of a Brahmin.
One certainly incurs a sin here equal to the killing of a Brahmin;
therefore, the sacred thread (yajñasūtra), provided with knots, is to be honored by all social classes. || 26 ||
But he who, having performed a sacrifice, does not indeed sprinkle the earth with milk, goes to the Taptabhūmi hell, tormented for seven lifetimes. (27)
Indeed, he who digs into the earth during an earthquake or an eclipse will certainly become a great sinner in another birth and be deprived of his limbs. (28)
Because it is the place where all beings dwell, it is proclaimed by him as "Bhūmi" (the Earth).
It is "Kāśyapī," belonging to Kaśyapa, and it is "Acalā" (Immovable) due to its stable nature. || 29 ||
O great sage, she is called Viśvambharā because she sustains the universe; Anantā because her nature is infinite; Pṛthivī because she is the daughter of Pṛthu; and Mahī because of her vast extent.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Attainment of the Fruits of Hell," in the Earth Narrative within the ninth book of the glorious *Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa*, a compendium of eighteen thousand verses.
The Description of the Legend of Gaṅgā. Nārada said: 1. [Nārada said: "The Description of the Legend of Gaṅgā. Nārada said: [1]
I have heard the narrative concerning the Earth, which is exceedingly captivating.
O best among the knowers of the Vedas, tell now the legend of Gaṅgā.
In Bhārata, that sovereign goddess departed due to the curse of Bhāratī.
She is the supreme embodiment of Viṣṇu herself, known as Viṣṇupadī. ||2||
How, in which age, and by whom was she formerly entreated and impelled?
I desire to hear that sequence, which destroys sins, bestows merit, and is auspicious.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
The illustrious Sagara, born of the solar dynasty, was a sovereign lord of kings.
He had two beautiful wives, Vaidarbhī and Śaibyā.
And to his wife was born a single son who was exceedingly charming.
Known as Asamañja, he was the increaser of the lineage born of Śaibyā.
And another woman, desiring a son, propitiated Śaṅkara.
And by the boon of Hara, a fetus was formed within her.
And when a hundred years had passed, she gave birth to a mere lump of flesh.
Seeing that, she meditated upon Śiva and wept aloud again and again.
Śambhu, assuming the form of a brāhmaṇa, went into his presence.
Having divided this lump, he distributed it into sixty thousand portions.
And all the sons became possessed of great strength and prowess.
Their bodies were scorched by the rays of the midday sun in the summer heat.
And due to the curse of the sage Kapila, they were reduced to ashes.
Hearing that, the king wept and went into the dense forest.
Asamañja performed incomparable austerities for the purpose of bringing down the Gaṅgā.
Having performed austerities for a hundred thousand years, he died due to the course of time.
Aṃśumān was his son, [born] for the purpose of bringing the Gaṅgā.
Having performed austerities for a hundred thousand years, he died according to the course of time.
His son was Bhagīratha, a highly wise and great devotee of the Lord.
He is a devotee of Viṣṇu, a worshiper of Viṣṇu, virtuous, and free from old age and death.
Having performed austerities for a hundred thousand years for the purpose of bringing the Gaṅgā.
He beheld Kṛṣṇa, whose splendor was equal to ten million suns at the height of summer.
Having two arms, with a flute in his hand, and wearing the attire of a youthful cowherd boy.
He who has the form of Gopālasundarī, whose nature is to bestow grace upon his devotees. || 15 ||
The Supreme Brahman, consisting of His own will, the most perfect Lord.
It is praised by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others, and lauded by hosts of sages.
It is untainted, of the nature of a witness, devoid of qualities, and beyond primordial nature (prakṛti).
With a slight smile and a serene countenance, he acts for the sake of bestowing grace upon his devotees.
Wearing garments purified by fire and adorned with jewel ornaments.
Having seen him, the king bowed down again and again and offered praise.
And by his effortless play, he obtained the desired boon: the destruction of his lineage.
And having performed this divine hymn of praise, his body was covered with horripilation.
The Blessed One said:
"O Goddess of the gods, go quickly to Bhārata due to the curse of Bhāratī."
By my command, bring all the sons of Sagara here, surrounded by their attendants.
Purified by the wind of your touch, they shall go to my abode.
"and bearing my forms as I travel upon a divine chariot. (21)
They shall become my attendants, free from all affliction at all times.
Having completely severed the fruits of actions performed throughout birth after birth.
Whatever sin has been accumulated by men in Bhārata over ten million births—
"It is heard in the Śruti that [impurity] is destroyed by the touch of the wind from the Gaṅgā. (23)
From touching the Goddess, merit is tenfold; from seeing her, it is even greater than that.
Merely by bathing at Mausala on an ordinary day, for men—
It is heard in the Śruti that the sins of a hundred crore births are destroyed.
And whatever sins there may be, such as the killing of a Brahmin and so forth. || 25 ||
Those very [sins] accumulated over a multitude of births, even those committed through desire.
All of those perish for men through the ritual bath at Mausala.
